A hierarchical partitioning approach that subdivides blocks into convex subblocks to ensure meshlets do not exceed vertex/index constraints [S1].

The claim states that the approach uses hierarchical partitioning to subdivide blocks into convex subblocks to ensure meshlets do not exceed vertex/index constraints. The evidence explicitly confirms this in multiple places: 1) The notes list 'A hierarchical partitioning approach that subdivides blocks into convex subblocks to ensure meshlets do not exceed vertex/index constraints' as a key feature. 2) The text in Section 3.2.1 states: 'Our block-based region analysis kernel subdivides a block... so that meshlets extracted from each resulting subblock do not exceed vertex and index count constraints.' 3) It further clarifies: 'our region analysis kernel has the additional constraint that the subsequent meshlet extraction stage... works on convex subblocks'. 4) It describes the hierarchical nature: 'First, the kernel determines whether all isosurface geometry within the block can be represented by a single meshlet. If this is not the case, it determines whether the isosurface in each of the subblocks of size 4×4×4 can be represented by a single meshlet. Any of those subblocks that cannot be represented by one meshlet are further partitioned into 2 × 2 × 2 subblocks.' All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
supported

It replaces PMB's single compute shader with a task/mesh shader pair to reduce thread-level divergence, enable hierarchical partitioning via task shader tree-expansion, and allow asynchronous execution for pipeline overlap [S1].

The claim states that the method replaces PMB's single compute shader with a task/mesh shader pair to achieve three specific goals: 1) reduce thread-level divergence, 2) enable hierarchical partitioning via task shader tree-expansion, and 3) allow asynchronous execution for pipeline overlap. Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points in Section 3.2. It states that the approach replaces the compute shader with 'a coupled pair of task and mesh shaders'. It lists the reasons for this replacement, including: 'splitting the original PMB extraction into two tightly coupled kernels reduces thread-level divergence (TLD)', 'tree-expansion capabilities of task shaders make it possible to spawn multiple mesh shader workgroups, allowing us to divide extraction blocks into subblocks' (hierarchical partitioning), and 'task and mesh stages execute asynchronously, so mesh workgroups... can overlap with later analysis work, providing practical pipeline asynchrony'. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the method uses 'coupled task and mesh shaders' to extract meshlets from scalar volumes. It confirms that this approach addresses the 'lack of control over meshlet size constraints' found in the parent method, PMB (Poisson Meshlet-Based Extraction), by employing a hierarchical partitioning approach into convex subblocks (size-constrained meshlets) to ensure meshlets do not exceed vertex/index constraints.
